## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Nadīsota Sutta* ("A River", Iti 109) is a discourse situated in the fourth chapter of the *Itivuttaka* (It 4.10; PTS It 113). The text develops an extended metaphor illustrating the hazards of "going with the flow". In his study of early Buddhist concepts, Giuliano Giustarini observes that the *Nadīsotasutta* defines renunciation (*nekkhamma*) as "going against the stream" [Giustarini]. While renunciation literally signifies worldly abandonment—such as leaving the household life—the current of the river serves essentially as an image for craving (*taṇhā*), making outer renunciation a symbol for inner renunciation [Giustarini].

 Within the Pali canon, however, DharmaNexus detects widespread text reuse, identifying 181 matching passages across 22 different Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The sutta shares its longest and most substantial alignment with the *Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta* (SN 35, where segments 6.1–11.1 correspond closely to SN 35.238) [DharmaNexus]. Further notable text reuse appears in the *Catukkanipāta* (AN 4.63), the *Dvedhāvitakka Sutta* (MN 19), the *Vammika Sutta* (MN 23), other Majjhima Nikāya discourses (MN 12, MN 29, MN 30, MN 105), AN 6, AN 8, and the *Khaggavisāṇasuttaniddesa* (Cnd 23), as well as within the *Itivuttaka-aṭṭhakathā* and related commentarial literature [DharmaNexus].
